verdict.binding_term: COHERENT systematics (HI/gas calibration, local z=0 reference, lens-model magnification) -- NOT sample size, NOT the acceleration regime

caveats: The per-object redshift list, magnifications, velocities and gas masses of the 95 galaxies are NOT published as a table (Tables 1-3 of Jeanneau+2026 are kinematic priors, SED priors and TFR fit parameters). N(z) is therefore an ASSUMPTION here and is swept over three shapes (uniform / low-heavy / high-heavy). The upper-half information share moves only 67-75%, so no conclusion in this file depends on N(z).

sigma_V/V per object is NOT published; only the selection cut Delta v/v < 30% is. It is SWEPT 5-30% and every headline number states which value it used. The baryonic-mass uncertainty +/-0.2 dex IS published (adopted in the paper's own TFR fit).

MAGNIFICATION uncertainties are NOT propagated in the published analysis, so the published +/-0.06 dex stat error OMITS a term that this file computes to be 0.034-0.101 dex on log10 a0 after sqrt(4)-cluster averaging -- i.e. comparable to BAR-3S on its own. Any use of the +/-0.06 stat number as if it were a total error is therefore forbidden.

The MAGNIFICATION LEVER is (y+1) = 1.5477, NOT the 1:1 of the deep-MOND limit. Using 1:1 at this sample's y = 0.5477 would understate the mu term by 1.55x. The hostile (correct) value is used throughout.

The TREND route's coherent immunity is REAL but it is bought at a 3.61x smaller signal, and its viability is controlled ENTIRELY by the drift-exposure weight w for the z-DEPENDENT part of the Tacconi+2020 / NEUTRALUNIVERSEMACHINE gas prescriptions. The committed w = 0.20 was assigned for the ACCELERATION regime, not for that channel. At w = 0.20 the drift absorbs 23% of the trend and the route lives; at w = 1.00 it absorbs 94% and the route dies. This is the single most load-bearing unmeasured number in the file and it is flagged as such, not resolved in the framework's favour.

The HI nuisance is carried with prior M_HI in [0, M_mol], never zero, and it is SIGN-LOCKED toward RISE: under-counting M_bar makes a0 read HIGH. Its full range 0.262-0.509 dex on log10 a0 is 3.8-7.4x BAR-3S by itself. It works AGAINST the framework's declining branch and is carried anyway.

ESTIMATOR: median-like only. GLS is FORBIDDEN (committed estimator_bias_verdict.json: gls_origin bias +10.34 pp FAIL, theilsen_pairwise +7.93 pp FAIL; median_a0pt +0.84, ivw_median_a0pt +0.66, galaxy_median_then_median +0.31 pp PASS). The median's efficiency penalty sqrt(pi/2) = 1.2533 is APPLIED to every incoherent term, not waived.

z ~ 0.9 CANNOT test DEC vs FLAT: DEC(0.9) = 0.9996 against FLAT = 1, a 0.043% gap needing 0.0142% precision. Every result here is DEC-vs-RISE = de Sitter horizon vs Hubble horizon. A DEC win at z~0.9 refutes McCulloch's reading; it does NOT detect the framework's distinctive decline, which still needs z >~ 2.

The a0-LINE per-object route is 2.10x tighter per object than the bTFR route because the framework's kernel is exact at every radius. That is a genuine, framework-native gain and it is reported as such -- but it is a FORECAST for a re-analysis that does not exist yet, NOT a published capability of MUSE-DARK II.

BOTH FOOTINGS: canonical cH_Lambda/Z = 9.3550e-11 and alt cH0/Z = 1.1305e-10 give IDENTICAL numbers, because everything lives in the footing-independent ratio a0(z)/a0(0) (asserted numerically in S0). a0's VALUE and the HORIZON CHOICE remain POSITS.

nu = sqrt(1 + 1/y) is Milgrom 1999 (PLA 253:273 Eq.9) -- WELLHEAD CREDIT. The framework's distinctive content is the cH_Lambda/Z coefficient and the modified-inertia completion. McCulloch (MiHsC) credited for the Hubble-horizon branch. No TOE, no 'theory closed', no closed doors. Exit 0 = ran, NOT a verdict.
